stories.headline: Floods leave AP-Odisha border villages inundated, traffic on NH-16 disrupted
stories.title: Flash floods leave AP-Odisha border villages inundated, traffic on NH-16 disrupted
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Life has become miserable for thousands of people living in Ichchapuram and surrounding villages, including Loddaputti, Korigam, Rattakanna and others, along the Andhra Pradesh- Odisha border, after flash floods inundated low-lying areas following surge of water in the Bahuda river and seasonal streams.
The flooding followed the release of large volume of water from the Baghalati Dam located in the Patrapur block of Odisha’s Ganjam district, inundating many border villages.
Traffic on National Highway-16, which connects Chennai-Kolkata was also disrupted by the overflowing river Bahuda and seasonal streams.
Odisha irrigation officials alerted their AP counterparts before releasing around 86,000 cusecs of water from the dam on Thursday afternoon.

The Srikakulam district administration had also taken steps to relocate people, but the evacuation was done only partially as it was late at night and there was no much time to inform all the villagers.
Power outages, lack of internet connectivity, added to the residents woes.
Streets in several villages turned into flowing streams, preventing people from moving to safer places.
“People living in Ichchapuram and surrounding villages were shocked with the sudden surge of floodwater at night.
In the absence of internet connectivity on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) night residents were unable to contact any official,” said Tarunraj, an advocate from Ichchapuram.
Former Ichchapuram MLA Piriya Sairaj alleged that the government had utterly failed in taking up adequate relief measures in the flood-affected areas.

Srikakulam District Congress Committee president Sanapala Annaji Rao said that the government could have averted inundation of the villages if it had properly coordinated with the Odisha administration.
Meanwhile, the administration sent National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), and special teams to the border town, which is almost 120 km from Srikakulam district headquarters.

stories.headline: Jal Shakti Minister CR Patil reviews Ganga basin flood control initiatives
stories.title: Jal Shakti Minister CR Patil reviews Ganga basin flood control initiatives
stories.summary: Union Jal Shakti Minister C.R. Patil reviewed the planning and implementation of measures to address flood, erosion and drainage problems in the Ganga basin during the 19th meeting of the Ganga Flood Control Board (GFCB), an official said on Thursday.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Union Jal Shakti Minister C.R. Patil reviewed the planning and implementation of measures to address flood, erosion and drainage problems in the Ganga basin during the 19th meeting of the Ganga Flood Control Board (GFCB), an official said on Thursday.

New Delhi: Union Jal Shakti Minister C.R. Patil reviewed the planning and implementation of measures to address flood, erosion and drainage problems in the Ganga basin during the 19th meeting of the Ganga Flood Control Board (GFCB), an official said on Thursday.

Patil led discussions on preparation of risk-based basin Master Plans, assessment of the adequacy of waterways and ventways under bridges, improving the quality of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), timely implementation of flood management projects and application of modern technologies in flood management, the official said in a statement.

During the review meeting held on Tuesday, the Union Minister emphasised coordination among Union Ministries, state governments and other stakeholders, particularly in addressing issues relating to river morphology, drainage congestion, infrastructure development and flood resilience, the statement said.

The meeting reaffirmed the importance of an integrated, risk-informed and technology-enabled approach to flood management, supported by effective Centre–state cooperation, improved technical standards and coordinated implementation of flood management measures across the Ganga basin, it added.

The Union Minister also highlighted importance of modern survey techniques, sound technical investigations, appropriate statutory clearances and timely resolution of project implementation bottlenecks.

"The meeting was attended by Suvendu Adhikari, Chief Minister of West Bengal; Ram Nath Thakur, Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; K. V. Raju, NITI Aayog member; Vijay Kumar Choudhary, Bihar Deputy Chief Minister and Water Resources Minister; Swatantra Dev Singh, Uttar Pradesh Jal Shakti Minister; representatives of the Ganga basin states; senior officials of the Central and state governments; and representatives of the concerned agencies," the statement said.
The Board, chaired by the Union Jal Shakti Minister, provides a high-level institutional platform for strengthening Centre–state cooperation and coordinated flood management across the Ganga basin.

The meeting chaired by C.R. Patil on Tuesday provided an opportunity to review ongoing initiatives, strengthen interstate coordination and deliberate upon emerging approaches for effective flood management.

The Board, constituted by the Union government on April 18, 1972, comprises representatives of the concerned Central Ministries and Chief Ministers of the Ganga Basin states or their representatives, with the Ganga Flood Control Commission (GFCC) Chairman Er.
Sher Singh, serving as its Member Secretary, the statement said.

stories.headline: Why investors may have to navigate volatility in the capital markets
stories.title: Why investors may have to navigate volatility in the capital markets
stories.summary: With oil prices rising, monetary policy tightening and domestic demand remaining fragile, investors may have to navigate a period of heightened volatility in capital markets. Persistent global, geopolitical and macroeconomic headwinds are also adding to the uncertainty, keeping markets on edge.“After touching an all-time high in September 2024, the Indian equity markets have undergone a prolonged phase of consolidation, marked by both time and price correction,” says Deven Mistry, analyst, Motilal Oswal Financial Services.The surge in global 10-year bond yields and re-emergence of a rate-hike cycle are some of the key concerns for equities. The US Fed has raised rates by 25 basis points to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first hike in three years, while the Bank of Japan has raised rates twice to 1.25 percent and the European Central Bank by 25 bps to 2.25 percent. In India, too, the cost of capital has risen, with the Reserve Bank of India raising the repo rate by 25 bps and shifting its stance to ‘calibrated tightening’. Members cited rising inflationary pressures and firm growth as reasons for the hike.Also Read: Markets crash: Is this a perfect storm or just panic?“The spike in global bond yields to a two-decade high is particularly concerning, as tighter financial conditions and the increasing relative attractiveness of developed markets could divert capital flows away from emerging markets,” Mistry says.He explains that the sharp rise in global bond yields to multi-decade highs, alongside a potential shift towards a higher-for-longer rate environment, could encourage global investors to rotate towards fixed income and away from emerging-market equities. A sustained rise in global yields could, therefore, remain a key headwind for the equity markets.However, that’s not all. Supply shocks, rising global debt and inflationary pressures have also rattled sentiment. At the same time, the AI-led technology boom, along with the infrastructure and capital expenditure cycle supporting it, is attracting a disproportionate share of global capital flows, reshaping investment priorities across markets.Crude oil sits at the heart of the risk matrix. Higher prices, fuelled by geopolitical tensions, threaten to widen India’s import bill, stoke inflation and weigh on both the rupee and corporate profitability. Any escalation involving Iran, the Strait of Hormuz or regional energy assets could amplify market concerns. A sustained correction in oil prices, however, would ease pressure on macroeconomic fundamentals and provide a supportive backdrop for financial markets.WTI crude surged past $100 a barrel, while Brent remained above $110 in October, as escalating tensions in the Middle East raised concerns over prolonged energy supply disruptions following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.However, valuations in Indian markets have not cooled off yet. “Two years of flat markets, despite earnings growth, have erased the valuation excesses of Indian equities. But rates have moved up too. In fact, relative to bonds, valuations are still around their 2024 peak, with earnings headwinds rising,” says Prateek Parekh, equity strategist at Nuvama Institutional Equities. The NSE 500’s one-year forward price-to-earnings ratio is now 18 times, in line with its 20-year average, versus 24x in September 2024, while the five-year rolling CAGR is now just 9 percent.Also Read: Red-hot market debut: Jio Platforms lists at 21% premiumEl Niño risksWeather risks, particularly deficient rainfall and the adverse effects of the El Niño, are likely to weigh on crops and rural demand, and stoke inflation. With the 2026 monsoon being the weakest in over a decade, all eyes are now on the kharif harvest and rabi sowing. With the super El Niño expected to peak by year-end, the weather overhang around winter sowing continues to linger.“As the rainfall outcome came in lower-than-estimated and the El Niño overhang persisted, concerns around kharif sowing, harvest, a likely supply shock translating into price shock gained momentum. A similarly tough backdrop exists as rabi sowing is about to begin,” says Aastha Gudwani, India chief economist, Barclays.The monsoon ended with rainfall at 88 percent of the long-period average (LPA), not only below normal but also below the India Meteorological Department’s forecast of 90 percent of the LPA.Spatially, 16 out of 36 subdivision recorded ‘deficient’ rainfall; overall, 25 out of 35 states and Union Territories received rainfall below the LPA, of which, 17 states recorded ‘deficient’ rainfall.Gudwani adds that rural consumer sentiment has deteriorated further by the end of the monsoon season. An analysis of company earnings transcripts for Q1 FY27 and early commentary from Q2 shows that rural consumption has maintained momentum in select sectors (such as agri machinery, auto), while others (like consumer staples) have seen income uncertainty affecting demand. El Niño also featured multiple times in the transcripts as a potential headwind for rural demand through its impact on agricultural output.“We note a softening of sentiment versus Q4 FY26 results, when firms appeared more upbeat on rural consumption citing improved farm and non-farm incomes (from a healthy crop season in FY26), government welfare spending and GST rationalisation. While rural demand growth generally outpaced urban consumption over the last year, as per company reports, the commentary on distinct outperformance in the rural segment appeared missing or was somewhat diluted in latest quarterly earnings reports,” Gudwani says.Vinod Karki, equity strategist at ICICI Securities, also feels that as several states have slipped into deficient rainfall territory, it is casting a cloud over rural demand and investor sentiment.A few state governments like Maharashtra and Karnataka have announced support towards drought-relief measures. “At this juncture, there is no expectation of loan waiver schemes or large bailout packages. However, it is likely that more government support measures could be announced to support farmers facing drought situation,” Karki says.He adds that, in certain states, non-performing assets from agricultural loans are likely to rise, gaining prominence as a key metric to gauge stress levels arising from the drought.

opening: With oil prices rising, monetary policy tightening and domestic demand remaining fragile, investors may have to navigate a period of heightened volatility in capital markets.
Persistent global, geopolitical and macroeconomic headwinds are also adding to the uncertainty, keeping markets on edge.
body: “After touching an all-time high in September 2024, the Indian equity markets have undergone a prolonged phase of consolidation, marked by both time and price correction,” says Deven Mistry, analyst, Motilal Oswal Financial Services.
The surge in global 10-year bond yields and re-emergence of a rate-hike cycle are some of the key concerns for equities.

The US Fed has raised rates by 25 basis points to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first hike in three years, while the Bank of Japan has raised rates twice to 1.25 percent and the European Central Bank by 25 bps to 2.25 percent.
In India, too, the cost of capital has risen, with the Reserve Bank of India raising the repo rate by 25 bps and shifting its stance to ‘calibrated tightening’.
Members cited rising inflationary pressures and firm growth as reasons for the hike.

“The spike in global bond yields to a two-decade high is particularly concerning, as tighter financial conditions and the increasing relative attractiveness of developed markets could divert capital flows away from emerging markets,” Mistry says.

He explains that the sharp rise in global bond yields to multi-decade highs, alongside a potential shift towards a higher-for-longer rate environment, could encourage global investors to rotate towards fixed income and away from emerging-market equities.
A sustained rise in global yields could, therefore, remain a key headwind for the equity markets.
However, that’s not all.
Supply shocks, rising global debt and inflationary pressures have also rattled sentiment.

At the same time, the AI-led technology boom, along with the infrastructure and capital expenditure cycle supporting it, is attracting a disproportionate share of global capital flows, reshaping investment priorities across markets.
Crude oil sits at the heart of the risk matrix.
Higher prices, fuelled by geopolitical tensions, threaten to widen India’s import bill, stoke inflation and weigh on both the rupee and corporate profitability.
Any escalation involving Iran, the Strait of Hormuz or regional energy assets could amplify market concerns.
A sustained correction in oil prices, however, would ease pressure on macroeconomic fundamentals and provide a supportive backdrop for financial markets.

WTI crude surged past $100 a barrel, while Brent remained above $110 in October, as escalating tensions in the Middle East raised concerns over prolonged energy supply disruptions following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
However, valuations in Indian markets have not cooled off yet.
“Two years of flat markets, despite earnings growth, have erased the valuation excesses of Indian equities.
But rates have moved up too.
In fact, relative to bonds, valuations are still around their 2024 peak, with earnings headwinds rising,” says Prateek Parekh, equity strategist at Nuvama Institutional Equities.
The NSE 500’s one-year forward price-to-earnings ratio is now 18 times, in line with its 20-year average, versus 24x in September 2024, while the five-year rolling CAGR is now just 9 percent.
El Niño risksWeather risks, particularly deficient rainfall and the adverse effects of the El Niño, are likely to weigh on crops and rural demand, and stoke inflation.
With the 2026 monsoon being the weakest in over a decade, all eyes are now on the kharif harvest and rabi sowing.
“As the rainfall outcome came in lower-than-estimated and the El Niño overhang persisted, concerns around kharif sowing, harvest, a likely supply shock translating into price shock gained momentum.
A similarly tough backdrop exists as rabi sowing is about to begin,” says Aastha Gudwani, India chief economist, Barclays.

Spatially, 16 out of 36 subdivision recorded ‘deficient’ rainfall; overall, 25 out of 35 states and Union Territories received rainfall below the LPA, of which, 17 states recorded ‘deficient’ rainfall.
Gudwani adds that rural consumer sentiment has deteriorated further by the end of the monsoon season.

An analysis of company earnings transcripts for Q1 FY27 and early commentary from Q2 shows that rural consumption has maintained momentum in select sectors (such as agri machinery, auto), while others (like consumer staples) have seen income uncertainty affecting demand.
El Niño also featured multiple times in the transcripts as a potential headwind for rural demand through its impact on agricultural output.

“We note a softening of sentiment versus Q4 FY26 results, when firms appeared more upbeat on rural consumption citing improved farm and non-farm incomes (from a healthy crop season in FY26), government welfare spending and GST rationalisation.

While rural demand growth generally outpaced urban consumption over the last year, as per company reports, the commentary on distinct outperformance in the rural segment appeared missing or was somewhat diluted in latest quarterly earnings reports,” Gudwani says.
Vinod Karki, equity strategist at ICICI Securities, also feels that as several states have slipped into deficient rainfall territory, it is casting a cloud over rural demand and investor sentiment.
A few state governments like Maharashtra and Karnataka have announced support towards drought-relief measures.
“At this juncture, there is no expectation of loan waiver schemes or large bailout packages.
However, it is likely that more government support measures could be announced to support farmers facing drought situation,” Karki says.
He adds that, in certain states, non-performing assets from agricultural loans are likely to rise, gaining prominence as a key metric to gauge stress levels arising from the drought.

stories.headline: Supreme Court calls for financial institutions to compensate digital arrest victims
stories.title: Supreme Court calls for financial institutions to compensate digital arrest victims
stories.summary: The Bench stressed that the proposed regulatory framework must provide for suitable compensation to victims where financial institutions are found to have failed in their due diligence obligations
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Observing that banks must be made accountable to indemnify losses of victims of digital fraud, the Supreme Court on Thursday (October 29, 2026) said victims of offences like digital arrests should receive compensation of at least the amount lost if the fraud is found to have resulted from a failure of due diligence by the financial institution.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said it would examine the Reserve Bank of India's proposed Know Your Customer (KYC) Amendment Directions, 2026, which are expected to be notified by November 30 and operationalised by December 31.
The Bench stressed that the proposed regulatory framework must provide for suitable compensation to victims where financial institutions are found to have failed in their due diligence obligations.

It also reiterated the need for mandatory preventive measures, including temporarily suspending unusual transactions that deviate from an account holder's established transaction pattern, automated reporting of suspicious activity and physical verification to establish the genuineness of transactions.
The Court further said that it is the responsibility of banks to alert neighbouring police stations about unusual transactions involving customers who may be victims of digital arrest scams.
The Bench asked the RBI to provide details of the financial institutions that would be covered by the proposed guidelines and the measures being considered to compensate victims for their losses.

During the hearing, Attorney General R. Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, informed the Court that reported digital arrest cases had declined by around 50% compared with the previous year, attributing the reduction to the Court's intervention, coordinated action by government ministries and departments, and public awareness campaigns.
The CJI, however, pointed out that the country had still suffered losses of nearly ₹800 crore from such offences this year.

The CJI identified two key areas requiring further intervention, the accountability of banks and the problem of mule accounts, which are frequently used to receive and transfer proceeds of cybercrime.

The matter, titled In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents, is being monitored by the Supreme Court as part of efforts to strengthen the country's institutional response to cyber-enabled financial fraud.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court Collegium has approved the proposal for appointment of nine advocates as Judges of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.
The decision was taken at a Collegium meeting held on October 29, 2026, according to a statement issued by the Supreme Court Collegium.
The recommendations follow an earlier exercise by the High Court Collegium, headed by Chief Justice Arun Palli, which had recommended 11 names for appointment as High Court Judges in April this year.
The recommendations comprised 10 advocates from the Bar quota and one judicial officer from the Bench quota.
The earlier recommendations were part of an exercise to address vacancies in the High Court, whose sanctioned strength had been increased from 17 to 25 Judges in November 2024.

article_sentences: The Tamil Nadu Cabinet, headed by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, on Thursday approved a structured package of incentives for eight new industrial companies setting up or expanding projects across Coimbatore, Krishnagiri, Kanchipuram, Chengalpattu and Erode districts, involving investments of ₹3,767 crore and generating employment opportunities for 4,853 people.
The proposed projects span emerging sectors, including technical textiles, aerospace and defence, life sciences and electronics, among others, according to sources.
The Cabinet also approved the expansion plans of three companies.
The government did not disclose the names of the companies or provide a district-wise break-up of the investments and employment generation.
Separately, the Cabinet approved a proposal to constitute a multi-member commission, headed by a retired High Court judge, to conduct the Social Justice Survey.
Briefing the media after the Cabinet meeting, CTR Nirmal Kumar said the survey was one of the key poll promises of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) ahead of the 2026 Assembly election.
The Governor’s inaugural address to the State Assembly had also referred to the proposal.
The survey is expected to be conducted next year, after the completion of the ongoing Census.
The commission to oversee the exercise will be constituted by February or March next year, he said.

stories.headline: Gold steady at Rs 1.46 lakh/10 gm in Delhi; silver rises Rs 500/kg
stories.title: Gold steady at Rs 1.46 lakh/10 gm in Delhi; silver rises Rs 500/kg
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 29: Gold prices were steady at Rs 1.46 lakh per 10 grams in the national capital on Thursday as jewellers and retailers remained cautious about fresh purchases amid elevated rates. Silver prices, however, rose by Rs 500 to Rs 1,98,500 per kilogram, inclusive of all taxes, according to the All India Sarafa Association. The white metal closed unchanged at Rs 1.98 lakh per kg on Wednesday. Traders said gold prices remained steady as jewellers and retailers were cautious about fresh buying amid high prices. "Domestic gold prices remained steady on Thursday, following range-bound movements in international markets amid mixed signals," said Saumil Gandhi, Senior Analyst of Commodities at HDFC Securities. A hawkish stance by the US Federal Reserve overshadowed support from a decline in US Treasury yields and crude oil prices, he said. In international markets, spot gold fell by USD 49.38, or 1.21 per cent, to USD 4,018.08 per ounce, while silver declined 3 per cent to USD 52.41 per ounce. "Gold remained under pressure to hover around USD 4,024 per ounce on Thursday, as the Federal Reserve's hawkish outlook and persistent energy-driven inflation strengthen expectations of further monetary policy tightening," said Vedika Narvekar, Research Analyst- Commodities & Currencies, Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers Ltd. Firm crude oil prices, uncertainty around the Fed's policy path and equity-market liquidations are adding to volatility, although geopolitical risks and central-bank buying may offer support, she said.

stories.headline: Karnataka High Court upholds acquisition of additional land for expansion of Bengaluru central prison
stories.title: Karnataka High Court upholds acquisition of additional land for expansion of Bengaluru central prison
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A Division Bench of the High Court of Karnataka upheld the final notification issued by the State government in 2013 acquiring additional lands in Naganathapura village for expanding the Bengaluru Central Prison at Parappana Agrahara.

The Bench comprising Justice D.K. Singh and Justice H. Shanthi Bhushan, while allowing the appeals filed by the State government, has set aside the May 2, 2025, judgement of a single judge bench, which had quashed the final notification issued in August 2013, under Section 6(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

The government, in 2012, issued preliminary notification for acquisition of additional lands to expand the prison, its infrastructure, including staff quarters, etc., and to maintain 200 meter buffer zone from the outer wall of the prison as per the prison norms.

Meanwhile, a Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) after considering the objections from the owners of the lands on the 2012 notification, submitted a report to the government pointing out difficulties to acquire those lands citing high cost of acquisition, existence of RCC buildings, residential layouts, a 220 KV high-tension power line, etc. The SLAO had also suggested to the government for utilising lands available with the Prisons Department at Devanahalli for construction of the prison.

However, the government, after considering the SLAO’s report, issued final notification in August, 2013, and the landowners challenged this notification before a single judge, who in May 2025 quashed the 2013 notification, had directed the government to reconsider the matter based on the report submitted by the SLAO and after considering the objections raised by the landowners.
Overturning single judge’s view, the Bench held that the SLAO’s report had indeed considered the landowners’ objections, including the availability of alternative land at Devanahalli.
The bench emphasised that the SLAO’s recommendations are not binding on the government while pointing out that the government has to independently apply its mind before issuing final notification.

The Bench also ruled that the government has latitude in determining the land required for a genuine public purpose, prison expansion, buffer-zone security, and staff quarters to address overcrowding of the existing prison facility exceeding 5,000 inmates.

the acquisition of the notified lands for the expansion of the existing Central Prison serves a bona fide public purpose and cannot be set aside merely on account of hyper-technicalities in the procedure, in the absence of any established violation of a mandatory statutory requirement,” the Bench said.

However, the Bench directed the government and its authorities to take necessary steps to address the existence of RCC buildings, residential layouts, engineering workshops and developed sites on the subject notified lands, as referred to in the SLAO’s 2013 report, in accordance with law.

stories.headline: India loses to Afghanistan in FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival in Baku
stories.title: India loses to Afghanistan in FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival in Baku
stories.summary: Mohammad Mustafa and Shahzada Sultani struck in the first half to put Afghanistan in control, while Nibas Meetei Wahengbam’s goal proved insufficient to prevent India from falling into the 85th-to-88th-place semifinals.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'world cup' in title weight 42
article_sentences: India lost 1-2 to Afghanistan in the quarterfinals for positions 81 to 88 in the FIFA Under-15 World Cup & Festival at the Hovsan Competition Complex Pitch 1A in Baku on Thursday.
The Blue Colts will now face Kazakhstan, which lost to Hungary, in the semifinals for positions 85 to 88 later in the day.
Afghanistan opened the scoring against the run of play through Mohammad Mustafa (15’) before Shahzada Sultani (27’) doubled the side’s advantage.
Nibas Meetei Wahengbam (36’) reduced the deficit, but the Blue Colts could not find an equaliser.
India began with attacking intent and created a succession of opportunities in the sixth minute.
R. Lalremruatfela delivered a low cross from the left that the Afghanistan goalkeeper spilt, but Victor Lalawmpuia could not react quickly enough to capitalise.
The Afghanistan defenders were unable to clear the danger, allowing Nibas to regain possession inside the penalty area.
His attempted lay-off eluded Lalawmpuia before the ball reached an unmarked Lalremruatfela, whose left-footed effort drew a diving save from the goalkeeper.
The Blue Colts threatened again in the ninth minute when Nibas threaded a fine through ball from the wing towards Lalawmpuia.
However, the Afghanistan goalkeeper read the danger and came forward to gather before the Indian attacker could reach it.
Despite India’s promising start, Afghanistan took the lead.
Sultani delivered a cross from the left into the penalty area, where Mustafa got away from his marker, Birjit Singh Amom, and connected with a right-footed volley to put his side ahead.

stories.headline: Banks must compensate digital fraud victims for loss if due-diligence failure established: SC
stories.title: Banks must compensate digital fraud victims for loss if due-diligence failure established: SC
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 29: The Supreme Court on Thursday said banks must be made accountable to indemnify losses suffered by digital fraud victims, who should receive compensation of at least the amount lost if an investigation establishes that the offence resulted from a failure of due diligence by the financial institutions. Observing that despite the fact that cyber crimes fell by 50 per cent, yet victims lost Rs 800 crore so far this year, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the proposed Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulatory framework must incorporate enforceable provisions for compensation, preventive intervention and institutional accountability. The CJI said the bench would first examine the proposed RBI Know Your Customer (KYC) Amendment Directions, 2026, before permitting the regulatory process to proceed. The directions are proposed to be notified by November 30 and operationalised by December 31. The bench emphasised that the framework must go beyond general advisories and establish clear obligations on financial institutions, along with consequences for non-compliance. "We emphasise that the regulatory measures proposed by the RBI must mandate financial institutions to indemnify victims of digital arrest or cyber fraud through suitable compensation, not less than the amount lost by the customer, where the fraud or crime is found to have resulted from a failure of due diligence by the financial institution," it said in its order. "These are all hypertechnical things. Unless there is a penal direction to these banks, they will never mend their ways," the CJI said. It also reiterated that banks must temporarily suspend transactions that are inconsistent with an account holder's established transaction history, automatically report suspicious activity and undertake physical verification wherever necessary to establish the genuineness of a transaction. "Fraud running into thousands of crores has taken place through digital arrest scams, and we are still unable to take very strong measures. Why can banks not be mandated to classify accounts into different groups? For individual account holders who have saved money over time, banks have the complete audit trail. They can use AI," the CJI said. The observations came during the hearing of the suo motu proceedings titled In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents, initiated to strengthen the institutional response to digital arrest scams and related cyber-enabled financial crimes. During the hearing, the CJI questioned why banks could not intervene when an account holder suddenly sought to transfer a substantial sum that bore little resemblance to the person's usual banking activity. Describing banks as a "protective umbrella" for vulnerable customers, the CJI said financial institutions possess information about their account holders, including their transaction histories, and should use that knowledge to prevent fraud before money leaves an account. He drew a distinction between commercial accounts, where transactions worth crores of rupees may be routine, and individual accounts belonging to retired persons or ordinary savers who typically withdraw relatively small amounts. "If that person suddenly seeks to transfer a large amount through RTGS, why can there not be intervention," the CJI asked. The bench suggested that financial institutions could classify accounts according to their nature and transaction patterns and deploy technology, including artificial intelligence, to identify deviations that may indicate coercion or fraud. It also called for a mechanism under which the nearest police station would be automatically alerted about suspicious high-value transactions involving customers potentially targeted by digital arrest fraudsters. Local police could then verify whether the account holder was knowingly initiating the transaction, it said. The CJI cautioned that retrospective investigations and reports would not be sufficient if institutions failed to prevent the transfer of funds in the first place. "A report would only be a post-mortem. We are concerned with prevention," he said. Attorney General R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, told the bench that substantial work had been undertaken to improve the detection of suspicious transactions and strengthen preventive mechanisms within the banking system. The CJI, however, questioned whether the proposed measures contained sufficiently strong accountability provisions and whether they would result in meaningful action against institutions that failed to comply. "What are the accountability clauses in the guidelines? If a bank fails to comply, what is its accountability," the CJI asked. He further questioned whether the proposed framework would require a bank to compensate a victim in cases of digital arrest fraud. The attorney general submitted that the RBI was examining banking liability and the liability of individual bank officials, including personal liability and criminal prosecution where an employee was found to have colluded in a fraud. "The regulation must include a liability clause. Otherwise, we will enforce it through a judicial order," the CJI said. The attorney general said that the government was not defending banking negligence or collusion and was examining the various aspects of prevention and accountability. The court emphasised that the RBI's proposed directions must spell out the extent of institutional liability, the safeguards available to customers and the process through which compliance would be enforced. The bench said it did not intend to require every individual bank to be impleaded in the proceedings. Instead, it directed the RBI to submit a list of all authorised financial institutions by the next hearing so that any directions issued by the court could apply across the sector. The CJI identified two areas requiring particular attention: the accountability of banks and the continued use of mule accounts to receive and transfer proceeds of cybercrime. Mule accounts, often operated or obtained through deceptive means, are used by fraudsters to move money between accounts and make the tracing and recovery of stolen funds more difficult. The bench also directed the law enforcement agencies of all states and Union territories to submit reports detailing FIRs registered in digital arrest scam cases and the investigations arising from them. The agencies have also been asked to provide suggestions for the prevention, detection and prosecution of such offences. The DGPs of all states and Union territories have been directed to ensure compliance. The reports must be submitted to the inter-departmental committee coordinating the government's response, with reports furnished to the court also being forwarded to the committee, the bench directed. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for WhatsApp, told the bench the platform had taken preventive measures, including action against 9,400 accounts, and would file an affidavit detailing the steps undertaken. He said the platform was working on software to identify suspicious accounts and warn users.

"Fraud running into thousands of crores has taken place through digital arrest scams, and we are still unable to take very strong measures.
Why can banks not be mandated to classify accounts into different groups?
For individual account holders who have saved money over time, banks have the complete audit trail.
They can use AI," the CJI said.
The observations came during the hearing of the suo motu proceedings titled.
In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents, initiated to strengthen the institutional response to digital arrest scams and related cyber-enabled financial crimes.

During the hearing, the CJI questioned why banks could not intervene when an account holder suddenly sought to transfer a substantial sum that bore little resemblance to the person's usual banking activity.

Describing banks as a "protective umbrella" for vulnerable customers, the CJI said financial institutions possess information about their account holders, including their transaction histories, and should use that knowledge to prevent fraud before money leaves an account.

He drew a distinction between commercial accounts, where transactions worth crores of rupees may be routine, and individual accounts belonging to retired persons or ordinary savers who typically withdraw relatively small amounts.
"If that person suddenly seeks to transfer a large amount through RTGS, why can there not be intervention," the CJI asked.

The bench suggested that financial institutions could classify accounts according to their nature and transaction patterns and deploy technology, including artificial intelligence, to identify deviations that may indicate coercion or fraud.

It also called for a mechanism under which the nearest police station would be automatically alerted about suspicious high-value transactions involving customers potentially targeted by digital arrest fraudsters.
Local police could then verify whether the account holder was knowingly initiating the transaction, it said.
The CJI cautioned that retrospective investigations and reports would not be sufficient if institutions failed to prevent the transfer of funds in the first place.
"A report would only be a post-mortem.
We are concerned with prevention," he said.

Attorney General R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, told the bench that substantial work had been undertaken to improve the detection of suspicious transactions and strengthen preventive mechanisms within the banking system.

The CJI, however, questioned whether the proposed measures contained sufficiently strong accountability provisions and whether they would result in meaningful action against institutions that failed to comply.
"What are the accountability clauses in the guidelines?
If a bank fails to comply, what is its accountability," the CJI asked.
He further questioned whether the proposed framework would require a bank to compensate a victim in cases of digital arrest fraud.

The attorney general submitted that the RBI was examining banking liability and the liability of individual bank officials, including personal liability and criminal prosecution where an employee was found to have colluded in a fraud.
"The regulation must include a liability clause.
Otherwise, we will enforce it through a judicial order," the CJI said.
The attorney general said that the government was not defending banking negligence or collusion and was examining the various aspects of prevention and accountability.

The court emphasised that the RBI's proposed directions must spell out the extent of institutional liability, the safeguards available to customers and the process through which compliance would be enforced.
The bench said it did not intend to require every individual bank to be impleaded in the proceedings.
Instead, it directed the RBI to submit a list of all authorised financial institutions by the next hearing so that any directions issued by the court could apply across the sector.
The CJI identified two areas requiring particular attention: the accountability of banks and the continued use of mule accounts to receive and transfer proceeds of cybercrime.
Mule accounts, often operated or obtained through deceptive means, are used by fraudsters to move money between accounts and make the tracing and recovery of stolen funds more difficult.

The bench also directed the law enforcement agencies of all states and Union territories to submit reports detailing FIRs registered in digital arrest scam cases and the investigations arising from them.
The agencies have also been asked to provide suggestions for the prevention, detection and prosecution of such offences.
The DGPs of all states and Union territories have been directed to ensure compliance.

The reports must be submitted to the inter-departmental committee coordinating the government's response, with reports furnished to the court also being forwarded to the committee, the bench directed.

Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for WhatsApp, told the bench the platform had taken preventive measures, including action against 9,400 accounts, and would file an affidavit detailing the steps undertaken.
He said the platform was working on software to identify suspicious accounts and warn users.

sentences.text: The directions are proposed to be notified by November 30 and operationalised by December 31.

New Delhi, Oct 29: The Supreme Court on Thursday said banks must be made accountable to indemnify losses suffered by digital fraud victims, who should receive compensation of at least the amount lost if an investigation establishes that the offence resulted from a failure of due diligence by the financial institutions.

Observing that despite the fact that cyber crimes fell by 50 per cent, yet victims lost Rs 800 crore so far this year, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the proposed Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulatory framework must incorporate enforceable provisions for compensation, preventive intervention and institutional accountability.

stories.headline: Bengaluru-based Inkle acquires Finally’s bookkeeping arm, expands team to 160
stories.title: Bengaluru-based Inkle acquires Finally’s bookkeeping arm, expands team to 160
stories.summary: Bengaluru-built, San Francisco-headquartered CPA firm Inkle has acquired Finally's bookkeeping division in an undisclosed all-cash deal, taking its team to about 160 people across five countries and extending it from startups to non-tech small businesses.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Bengaluru-built, San Francisco-headquartered CPA firm Inkle has acquired Finally's bookkeeping division in an undisclosed all-cash deal, taking its team to about 160 people across five countries and extending it from startups to non-tech small businesses.

San Francisco-headquartered Inkle, an AI-driven accounting and bookkeeping firm for US companies that develops its technology in Bengaluru, has purchased the bookkeeping arm of small-business finance platform Finally.
The price has not been revealed.
Inkle describes the deal as an all-cash asset purchase and says it is the company’s first acquisition.

Around 100 Finally employees based in the Dominican Republic, Colombia, Puerto Rico, Miami, Boca Raton and New York will join Inkle’s 60-member team in Bengaluru, comprising engineers, product designers, tax professionals and bookkeepers.
With a workforce of about 160 across five countries, Inkle says it can provide round-the-clock support to clients across the Americas and Asia.
Finally’s existing bookkeeping customers will continue working with their current teams, while accessing services through Inkle’s software.
The acquisition also changes who Inkle works for.
Until now, the firm’s clients have been mainly venture-backed startups.

Finally’s customers are largely non-tech small businesses, including contractors, clinics, restaurants, professional services firms and owner-operators, a group Inkle regards as the core of America’s employer base.
“Ranvir and I are delighted to announce Inkle’s first acquisition,” said Anand Krishna, co-founder and CEO of Inkle.
“Inkle is an American company that serves American small businesses, and it’s built in Bengaluru.
